stem: A 25-year-old sexually active man has 2 days of fever, burning on urination and perineal pain. He recently started a relationship with a new partner and has noticed a clear urethral discharge. Rectal examination finds a tender, boggy prostate.
oneliner: 25M + fever, dysuria, perineal pain, urethral discharge + new sexual partner + tender boggy prostate → organism?
ask: Which organism is the most likely cause?

whyNot.A: The leading cause of prostatitis in **men over 35**, not in a young sexually active man
whyNot.B: Follows **catheterization or instrumentation**; he has had none
whyNot.C: Causes **orchitis and parotitis**, not a boggy prostate with urethral discharge
whyNot.D: A cause of cystitis in **young women**, not male prostatitis

why: In a **sexually active man under 35**, prostatitis follows **urethritis** from **Chlamydia trachomatis** (or Neisseria gonorrhoeae). **E. coli** dominates in older men.

bug.name: Chlamydia trachomatis
bug.type: Obligate intracellular bacterium with no peptidoglycan; does not Gram stain well
bug.lab: Elementary body infects and reticulate body replicates; Giemsa-stained inclusions in cells; detected by nucleic acid amplification
bug.virulence: Elementary body enters cells and blocks phagolysosome fusion; no cell wall peptidoglycan, so beta-lactams work poorly
bug.spread: Sexual contact; vertical to newborns during birth
bug.causes: Urethritis, cervicitis, PID, epididymitis, prostatitis in young men, neonatal conjunctivitis and pneumonia, trachoma (A-C), lymphogranuloma venereum (L1-L3)

idea.rule: Prostatitis follows the organisms common to age: sexually transmitted below 35, enteric above.
also: Neisseria gonorrhoeae also causes it in young men
E. coli in men over 35 and after instrumentation
Epididymitis follows the same age split

stem: A 33-year-old man returns from a trip abroad with a very painful genital ulcer that has soft, ragged, undermined edges and a gray, pus-covered base. A tender, fluctuant swelling has developed in his right groin. Gram stain of the ulcer exudate shows gram-negative rods lined up in chains.
oneliner: 33M + recent travel + painful soft ragged ulcer with gray base + tender fluctuant inguinal node + gram-negative rods in chains → organism?
ask: Which organism most likely caused the ulcer?

whyNot.A: Causes a **painless, clean-based** chancre; spirochetes are not seen on Gram stain
whyNot.B: Gives a **painless, beefy-red** ulcer (granuloma inguinale) with Donovan bodies
whyNot.D: Gives a **small, painless** ulcer followed by matted nodes, not a painful ragged ulcer
whyNot.E: Makes **grouped painful vesicles** that ulcerate; not a ragged ulcer with a suppurative bubo

why: A **painful ulcer with ragged edges and gray exudate** plus a **tender suppurating inguinal node (bubo)** is **chancroid**. Gram-negative coccobacilli in chains (**school of fish**) point to **Haemophilus ducreyi**.

bug.name: Haemophilus ducreyi
bug.lab: Needs hemin (factor X) but not NAD (factor V); grows on enriched chocolate agar; appears as a school of fish in chains on Gram stain
bug.virulence: Cytolethal distending toxin and hemolysin damage tissue; surface proteins resist phagocytosis
bug.spread: Sexual contact; more common in tropical regions
bug.causes: Chancroid: painful soft genital ulcer with a tender suppurative inguinal lymph node (bubo)

idea.rule: Painful genital ulcer with a suppurative bubo means chancroid; painless ulcers point elsewhere.
also: Lymphogranuloma venereum: transient painless ulcer, then matted nodes
Granuloma inguinale: painless beefy ulcer, Donovan bodies
